case_title: M N G Bharateesh Reddy v. Ramesh Ranganathan and Another
trial_court_outcome: Sessions Judge set aside the order of the Magistrate
high_court_outcome: High Court held that no case was made out against the General Manager under ss.499 and 500 of the IPC however, there were material on record which prima facie disclosed the offences u/ss.405 and 420 of the IPC
neutral_facts: The accused, a Consultant Neurosurgeon, was employed by a hospital under a consultancy agreement. He was terminated for inconsistent and unsatisfactory behavior. He filed a complaint alleging that the hospital management misused their authority and terminated his services with an ulterior motive. The complaint included allegations of improper billing and financial loss. The trial court dismissed the complaint, stating it did not disclose the ingredients of the offences of defamation or cheating. The High Court held that there was no case made out against the accused under sections 499 and 500 of the IPC, but there were material on record which prima facie disclosed the offences under sections 405 and 420 of the IPC. The Supreme Court, however, held that the allegations did not establish the necessary ingredients of the offences of cheating or criminal breach of trust, as there was no clear case of entrustment or fraudulent intent.
